oneLiner: The cleanest AI monetization print among hyperscalers - Azure past $100B and Copilot inflecting - at a premium multiple that assumes the capex stays pre-sold.
thesis: Azure is a $100B business still accelerating. +43% YoY in Q4 FY26 and +41% for the full fiscal year - the fastest-growing of the big three clouds.
Contracted demand de-risks the buildout. Commercial RPO of $678B, +84% YoY - still +25% excluding OpenAI commitments.

Copilot hit an inflection. Paid seats passed 30M (from ~20M in Q3 FY26), net adds more than doubled QoQ and Copilot revenue accelerated >60% QoQ - at only ~6.5% penetration of a ~464M-seat M365 commercial base.
OpenAI economics crystallized. An uncapped 27% stake worth ~$228B at OpenAI's $852B March 2026 valuation, plus $24.1B of FY26 revenue from OpenAI itself.
Margins expanding through the buildout. FY26 revenue +18% to $331.8B, operating income +21% to $155.2B, net income +31%, headcount -2%.

latestProse: Q4 FY26 (ended June 30, 2026): revenue $90.0B, +18% YoY; GAAP net income $35.8B, +31%; EPS $4.81 GAAP / $4.74 non-GAAP vs ~$4.24 expected. Azure grew 43% and crossed $100B in annual revenue (+41% for FY26); Microsoft Cloud hit $59.3B (+27%), ~90% of it from customers outside frontier-model companies. Intelligent Cloud ($39.3B, +32%) overtook Productivity ($37.8B, +14%); More Personal Computing fell 4%. FY26 closed at $331.8B revenue with $133.7B net income. The disclosure that matters most: commercial RPO of $678B (+84%) - while Microsoft pointedly declined to refresh April's $37B AI run-rate figure.
guidanceProse: Q1 FY27 guide: revenue $89.85-90.95B (+16-17%), Intelligent Cloud $40.95-41.25B, capex over $50B. FY27 capex was guided only qualitatively - it 'will grow year-over-year' - and the widely quoted $255-260B FY27 figure is an analyst preview, not company guidance. The headline debate is the accounting change: extending data-center/office useful life from 15 to 25 years shifts future finance leases to operating leases, trimming the reported CY2026 capex plan to ~$175B from ~$190B with, per CFO Hood, no change in actual spend - better optics, identical buildout.

segments: Q4 FY26 mix: Intelligent Cloud $39.3B (44% of revenue, +32%); Productivity & Business Processes $37.8B (42%, +14%); More Personal Computing $12.9B (14%, -4%)
Microsoft Cloud: $59.3B in Q4 (+27%); $214B+ for FY26
competitive: Cloud infrastructure share (Q1 2026): AWS ~30%, Azure ~25%, Google Cloud ~13% - Azure growing fastest of the three (43% vs AWS ~19%)
Copilot vs Google Workspace/Gemini in productivity AI; GitHub Copilot (50M users) vs Cursor and other AI coding tools
OpenAI is simultaneously partner, tenant, investee and rival - exclusivity and revenue-share economics restructured October 2025 and April 2026
Anthropic partnership hedges model dependency ($3.2B investment gain booked in Q4)
moat: Enterprise distribution: ~464M M365 commercial seats, identity/Teams lock-in, and compliance-grade trust let Microsoft attach AI to workflows it already owns. $678B of contracted RPO plus a capacity base that added 88 data centers in FY26 gives demand visibility and scale economics only AWS can rival.
risks: Free cash flow compression. FY26 capex was $115.9B with Q1 FY27 guided above $50B; Q4 FCF was just $19.6B, down YoY.
Accounting optics invite scrutiny. The 15-to-25-year useful-life extension cuts reported capex ~$15B and defers depreciation - bears read it as earnings-quality erosion timed to the spend peak.
OpenAI concentration and circularity. $24.1B of FY26 revenue from one loss-making customer; RPO grows 84% with OpenAI but 25% without.
Copilot could stall at shallow penetration - ~6.5% of the installed base three years after launch; GitHub's June 2026 shift to usage-based billing flatters the >60% QoQ growth.
Azure law of large numbers plus power/GPU constraints as Microsoft tries to double capacity in two years.
Valuation leaves little slack. ~24-25x forward with a slightly negative trailing-year return shows the multiple derates quickly on AI-capex anxiety.
catalysts: Late Oct 2026: FY27 Q1 earnings - first print under the new capex accounting
Sept-Dec 2026: unified Copilot 'super app' (including Code) promised to ship this quarter, per Nadella
Ongoing 2026-27: OpenAI compute and valuation milestones flowing into RPO and equity-method results
pricedIn: MSFT trades around $500-505 (Aug 2026; ~$3.74T market cap), roughly 24-25x forward consensus - a premium to Meta and Alphabet but below its 52-week high of $553.72, with a slightly negative trailing-year return after a spring AI-capex derating and a 7-8% post-earnings rebound. The price embeds durable ~40% Azure growth and rising Copilot attach. The Aug 2026 debate: does $678B of RPO make the capex effectively pre-sold, or do OpenAI circularity and lease-reclass optics overstate the quality of that visibility?

scenarios.bear: AI demand digests: Azure decelerates toward 30%, Copilot adds slow, and OpenAI strains under its compute obligations, turning RPO visibility into concentration risk. Depreciation catches up, EPS growth slows to single digits and the multiple contracts to ~20x: $400-430.
scenarios.base: Azure sustains high-30s growth on contracted backlog, Copilot seats keep compounding, and FCF troughs then recovers as the capex curve flattens; EPS grows mid-teens. The multiple holds ~24-25x: $550-600 over 12 months.
scenarios.bull: Copilot penetration triples toward 20% of the M365 base, the super app consolidates AI usage, Azure holds 40%+ toward a $150B year, and the ~$228B OpenAI stake plus Anthropic exposure earn explicit sum-of-parts credit: $650+.

valPresets.note: Basis is forward earnings: FY26 capex of $115.9B compresses FCF well below earnings power, and the useful-life accounting change further muddies cash-flow comparability.
